sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Redis and caching interview questions test whether you understand caching as a system, not just a library — Redis data structures (strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams, HyperLogLog), eviction policies (LRU, LFU, allkeys vs volatile), persistence (RDB, AOF), replication and Sentinel/Cluster modes, cache-aside vs read-through vs write-back, distributed locking (Redlock and its critics), and the common pitfalls (cache stampede, hot keys, big keys). This page is the one to use for any role that mentions Redis or distributed caching.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Redis is a **single-threaded in-memory data structure server** — speed comes from O(1) ops + simple ops.

- Data structures: strings / hashes / lists / sets / sorted sets / streams / HyperLogLog / bitmaps.
- Persistence: **RDB** (snapshot) + **AOF** (log) — combine for durability + recovery speed.
- HA: **Sentinel** for failover, **Cluster** for sharding.
- **Cache patterns** — cache-aside (default), read-through, write-back; pick by tolerance for stale data.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Cache stampede** — solve with mutex / probabilistic early-expiry / request coalescing.
- **Hot keys** — split with hash tags or local read-replicas.
- **Big keys** are the silent latency killer — set a max size in code.
- **Eviction** — LRU/LFU per-key; `volatile-*` only on TTL-set keys.
- **Distributed locking with Redlock** — Martin Kleppmann's critique is fair-game knowledge.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd cache <entity> via cache-aside with TTL <X>, tolerate eventual consistency on writes via <write-through | invalidation pattern>, pick the data structure as <hash for fielded reads | sorted set for leaderboards>, and guard against stampede with <single-flight + soft TTL>."*
